summary: A quantum dial is a tunable on-chip band-stop filter integrated with a dc SQUID array that dynamically modulates qubit–environment coupling by several orders of magnitude on nanosecond timescales, enabling fast switching between isolation (T₁ > 150 µs), resonant control (99.9% gate fidelity at 40 ns, −110 dBm), and dissipative reset (T₁ ≈ 200 ns, >97% ground-state population in 1.2 µs from |e⟩, |f⟩, |h⟩). The same device performs near-Cramér–Rao-bound qubit thermometry with noise-equivalent temperature of 0.6 mK/√Hz at 60 mK, unifying reset, control, and readout functions on a single tunable transmission line without separate dissipative elements.
motivation: Superconducting qubits require both long coherence times (demanding weak coupling) and fast control/reset (demanding strong coupling), a fundamental tension addressed only partially by existing Purcell filters and separate subsystems. Dynamic environmental engineering on nanosecond timescales offers an attractive solution to this isolation-and-control challenge.
method: A quarter-wavelength transmission-line filter capacitively coupled to a transmon qubit is made frequency-tunable by inserting a series array of five dc SQUIDs (effective inductance 0.075 nH) at an optimized position along the line; fast-flux lines enable nanosecond switching between three configurations—idle (filter tuned to qubit frequency $f_q$ for voltage node, maximizing $T_1$), control (detuned for Rabi frequency 12.5 MHz with $T_1 = 14$ µs), and reset (minimum $T_1 = 238$ ns for sequential relaxation).
result: Static and dynamic dialing achieve $F_\mathrm{avg}^\mathrm{Cliff.} = 0.9987$ and $0.9986$ respectively; dynamic dialing yields 10× improvement in interleaved idle fidelity ($F_\mathrm{I} = 0.9998$); reset from |e⟩, |f⟩, |h⟩ reaches $P_g \gtrsim 0.97$ in 1.2 µs with decay times $T_1^{ge} = 238.2 ± 3.3$ ns, $T_1^{ef} = 136.8 ± 2.8$ ns, $T_1^{fh} = 128.8 ± 3.4$ ns; thermometry precision approaches the four-level quantum Fisher information bound up to 400 mK.
